cf.title: Skip LEFT/ANTI joins to a provably empty inner rel

input.subject: Skip LEFT/ANTI joins to a provably empty inner rel

verdict_reasoning: No surviving objection is fatal, and none stops review at levels 1 or 2. Three fixable points remain: demand-1 asks for a realistic workload, standards-compat-1 asks whether the "stable" target means a back-patch, and maintenance-fit-3 asks for a comparison with a selectivity-only fix. A committer who knows outer-join Var handling has to judge whether the path substitution is safe. Confidence is low because only message #1 exists and no code was read.

brief.title: Skip LEFT/ANTI joins to a provably empty inner rel
brief.problem: When the inner side of a LEFT or ANTI join is proven empty, the planner still builds a real join against the dummy rel. The empty side is rescanned once per outer row, and a pushed-down "inner.x IS NULL" qual gets default selectivity (0.005), so the join is underestimated by orders of magnitude and the joins above it are planned badly.
brief.proposed_design: A new step in populate_joinrel_with_paths() handles JOIN_LEFT and JOIN_ANTI with a dummy inner rel when every pushed-down qual is "innervar IS NULL" and the reltarget can be computed from the outer rel alone. The join then takes the outer rel's size, and projections of all unparameterized and partial outer paths are added beside the regular join paths, so they must win on cost. FULL JOIN is not handled.
author_claims: Row estimates for such joins become correct, which avoids bad plans for the joins above them.
The example query drops from about 425 ms to about 150 ms, with a hash join replacing a nested loop over 1M rows.
Keeping all outer paths preserves sort orders, so ORDER BY ... LIMIT over an index still works.
Adding partial outer paths lets parallel plans avoid the per-row nested loop.
RIGHT joins are covered because they are planned as LEFT joins with the sides swapped.
brief.thread_state: Only the first message is visible. Nobody has replied yet.
unclear: The CommitFest entry targets "stable" but the proposal does not say whether a back-patch of a planner behaviour change is intended.
The proposal does not report planning-time cost for queries with many joins.
The proposal does not say whether quals other than "innervar IS NULL" were considered, such as quals that reference only outer Vars.
The regression tests cover only join.sql; the proposal does not say whether the all-partitions-pruned case is tested.
The proposal does not say how EXPLAIN output changes for users, given the join node disappears from the plan.
search_queries: partition pruning all partitions left join

objections.title: No real-world query shown that hits an empty inner rel
objections.failure_scenario: A committer adds a new path-generation step to populate_joinrel_with_paths() and owns its interaction with nulling relids, partial paths and setrefs. If few production queries ever reach a LEFT or ANTI join whose inner rel is dummy and whose pushed-down quals are all IS NULL, the project keeps that code and its corner cases for little gain.
objections.argument: The only demonstration in message #1 uses a literal "AND false" in the ON clause, which a user can remove by hand. The partition-pruning case is named in one sentence but has no example, plan or field report. No -general or -bugs report, no user request and no other database are cited, so the size of the user group is unknown. The FULL JOIN attempt in message #1 failed with "wrong varnullingrels", which shows this area has real correctness risk to set against the gain.
objections.author_must_show: Which real workloads, such as ORM-generated queries or LEFT JOINs to partitioned tables pruned to nothing, produce this plan shape, and how often do users report the bad estimate?

critic.reasoning: The only worked example uses a literal "AND false", and the partition-pruning case has no plan or report behind it. The failed FULL JOIN attempt is not part of this proposal and should not count as support; the request for demand evidence stands without it.

objections.title: CommitFest target "stable" implies a plan change in minor releases
objections.failure_scenario: A user applies a minor release that carries this patch. Row estimates for LEFT and ANTI joins to empty rels change, so the plans for the joins above them change too. A query that was tuned or stable on the old plan picks a different join order or method, and the user finds out from a regression in production after the upgrade.
objections.argument: CommitFest entry 7360 sets the target version to "stable". The patch changes cardinality estimates and adds new path candidates in populate_joinrel_with_paths(), and the before/after plans in message #1 show a different plan shape. Back branches normally avoid planner changes that alter plans for existing queries without a bug that produces wrong results. Message #1 and the commit message frame the change as a performance improvement and do not ask for a back-patch, so the target may be wrong.
objections.author_must_show: Is this intended for master only, and if a back-patch is wanted, what makes this estimate change a bug fix rather than a plan change for existing queries?

critic.reasoning: The CommitFest entry says "Target version: stable", and message #1 presents an optimization that changes estimates and plan shapes. The proposal does not say the patch is for master only, so the question stands as a fixable metadata point.

objections.title: A narrower estimate fix may give most of the gain
objections.failure_scenario: The project adds a second path-level form of join removal, next to the existing left-join removal in analyzejoins.c. Later, a planner developer changes join removal or outer-join estimation and has two separate places to keep consistent. Users see different plans depending on which mechanism handled the join.
objections.argument: Message #1 names the row estimate as "the bigger issue". The cost of rescanning a one-time-false Result for each outer row is small. Making the selectivity of an "innervar IS NULL" qual equal to 1 when the inner rel is dummy would fix the estimate in the example without adding joinrel paths. The proposal does not compare against that option or say what the path substitution adds beyond it.
objections.author_must_show: How much of the gain in the example remains if only the IS NULL selectivity over a dummy inner rel is corrected and no outer paths are added?

critic.reasoning: Message #1 calls the estimate "the bigger issue", and its own plan shows the left join taking about 38 ms of 425 ms. The proposal does not compare the path substitution with a selectivity-only fix, so the design question stands.

refuted.title: Target version "stable" implies back-patching a planner behaviour change
refuted.failure_scenario: A site with a tuned workload applies a minor release. Row estimates for its LEFT joins to pruned partitions jump from thousands to millions, and plans above them change. The site learns this from a production plan change after a minor upgrade, with no setting to restore the old plan.
refuted.argument: The CommitFest entry targets "stable", but message #1 and the commit message describe a new optimization, not a bug fix. Planner changes that alter estimates and plan shapes are normally kept to the master branch, because minor releases are expected to keep plans stable. The proposal does not say whether back-patching is intended or why this case would be an exception.
refuted.author_must_show: Is this intended for master only, and if not, what makes this estimate change safe to ship in a minor release?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1, which makes the same point and also allows that the target field may be a mistake.

refuted.title: Correctness depends on subtle nulling-relid reasoning in a new place
refuted.failure_scenario: A later patch changes how PlaceHolderVars or nulling bits appear in a join's reltarget. The outer rel's paths, substituted for the join, then emit Vars with the wrong varnullingrels. A user query fails at plan time with "wrong varnullingrels", and nothing in the new code catches the problem earlier.
refuted.argument: The proposal places outer-rel paths directly into a joinrel and relies on pull_varnos() reporting nulling relids to reject unsafe targets. Message #1 reports that the FULL JOIN version already failed in setrefs when the surviving side was a join or an Append. That shows how easily these assumptions break. Future work on outer-join Var handling must keep this shortcut in mind, and the only check is a setrefs error seen by users. The proposal does not say which invariants make the LEFT and ANTI cases safe when the outer side is itself a join, an Append, or contains PlaceHolderVars.
refuted.author_must_show: Which invariants guarantee that outer paths can emit the join's reltarget unchanged, and do the tests cover outer sides that are joins, Appends, or contain PlaceHolderVars?

critic.reasoning: Message #1 states the invariant: pull_varnos() of the reltarget, including nulling relids, must be a subset of the outer relids, and it explains why FULL JOIN breaks that. The scenario needs an unnamed future patch, and the setrefs check would fail loudly.

touch_points.label: planner behaviour change
touch_points.reason: The patch changes row estimates and adds outer-rel paths for LEFT and ANTI joins to a dummy inner rel.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The CommitFest entry sets the target version to "stable" for a change that alters plans.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: The new step in joinrels.c depends on nulling-relid rules that later outer-join work must keep in mind.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: The new check sits in populate_joinrel_with_paths(), and message #1 reports no planning-time numbers for queries with many joins.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Is the patch meant for master only, and if a back-patch is wanted, what makes this estimate change a bug fix?
Which real workloads reach a LEFT or ANTI join with a dummy inner rel, for example a partitioned table with every partition pruned by the ON clause?
How much of the gain in the example remains if only the IS NULL selectivity over a dummy inner rel is corrected and no outer paths are added?
What is the planning-time cost of the new step for queries with many joins that do not qualify?
Were pushed-down quals that reference only outer Vars considered, and why does the patch not handle them?

committability.owner_note: It needs a committer who knows the planner's join path generation and the nulling-relid rules for outer-join Vars. Nobody has replied to message #1 yet.
committability.liability: The owner signs for the correctness of using outer-rel paths as joinrel paths, including any later "wrong varnullingrels" failure. That liability lasts as long as the code stays.
committability.author_follow_up: No sign either way; the thread has only message #1.

priority.reason: The patch is about 11 KiB and changes one planner file plus tests, but its safety rests on nulling-relid rules that few reviewers know well. The only worked example uses a literal "AND false", so the number of affected users is unknown.

provisional_note: The code was not read, so this review could not check whether outer paths emit the join's reltarget correctly when the outer side is a join, an Append, or contains PlaceHolderVars. It also could not check test coverage for the all-partitions-pruned case.

precedents_retrieved.title: Remove LEFT JOINs in more cases
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets the planner remove a LEFT JOIN whose inner relation is unused even when the join can duplicate rows, if a DISTINCT or a GROUP BY without aggregates removes those duplicates again. It adds this check in join_is_removable() next to the existing unique-index and subquery proofs.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Antonin Houska's review found that the volatility checks miss some cases. A volatile function in a DISTINCT ON expression is not detected. The check of brel->lateral_vars does not look at the actual variables, so a lateral function referencing both sides of the join is not handled. The author returned the patch himself because the commitfest had no time left to address the review.
matched_queries: partition pruning all partitions left join
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Volatile function in the DISTINCT ON expression isn't necessarily noticed by your checks:

precedents_retrieved.title: INNER JOIN removals
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets the planner remove an inner-joined relation when none of its columns are used and a foreign key proves a matching row exists. Because pending foreign-key triggers can break that proof at run time, the planner builds two plans, one with the joins removed and one without, and an AlternativePlan node picks one at executor startup.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected to the design, the risk of bugs and the cost. The AlternativePlan node breaks the one-to-one match between plan trees and planstate trees, and calling make_one_rel() twice is unreliable because the planner changes its input data structures. He also doubted that "no pending AFTER trigger events" proves the foreign keys hold for the snapshot in use, and he noted new O(N^2) planning work and a pg_constraint lookup for every scanned relation.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I think it's a disaster from a system structural standpoint,
will probably induce nasty bugs, and simply doesn't apply to enough
real-world queries to be worth either the pain of making it work or the
planning overhead it will add.

precedents_retrieved.title: INNER JOIN removals
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch uses foreign key constraints to remove semi, anti and inner joins whose result is already guaranteed by the constraint. Because pending foreign key triggers can make such a removal wrong, the later versions plan the join normally and prune the unneeded join nodes at executor start-up when the trigger queue is empty.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author marked this entry rejected because it had become a duplicate. He had moved the patch to a new thread and a newer commitfest entry, where he said it was ready for review. Before that, Michael Paquier had proposed rejecting it because the last version still had FIXMEs and had seen no activity for months. The visible messages show no rejection of the design itself.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: There does not seem to be a delete button, so marking as "rejected" due to this now being a duplicate entry for this patch.

precedents_retrieved.title: Memoize ANTI and SEMI JOIN inner
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets the planner put a Memoize node on the parameterized inner side of a Nested Loop semi join or anti join, so pulled-up EXISTS and NOT EXISTS sublinks can reuse cached inner results. It relies on Memoize single-row mode, because each outer row needs only the first inner match.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Richard Guo showed that the change is unsafe for semi and anti joins unless the inner side is provably unique. Join clauses from an upper level can move to the semi join, so a second inner tuple arrives and fails with "cache entry already complete". A semi join with a provably unique inner is already reduced to an inner join, so the work narrowed to proving inner_unique for anti joins, and Richard Guo posted a patch for that. The visible messages do not show why the entry was then withdrawn.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I conducted some experiments, and I'm afraid it's not safe to consider Memoize for semi or anti joins, unless the inner side is provably unique.

precedents_retrieved.title: Remove ctid from self-join examples in UPDATE and DELETE docs
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes the self-join examples in the UPDATE and DELETE docs to join on an id column, not ctid. The author argues that a ctid self-join behaves like a join on a mutable column under concurrent updates, so readers could copy it to avoid deadlocks and lose updates without notice.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Only the author's first message is shown, with no replies, and the entry was later withdrawn.

precedents_retrieved.title: Improve join selectivity estimation using extended statistics
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch uses per-table extended statistics, mainly functional dependencies, when it estimates join selectivity in clausesel.c. It also tries to combine join clauses with relation-level filters in calc_joinrel_size_estimate to estimate conditional probabilities.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tomas Vondra found the design at the wrong level of abstraction. Clausesel.c handled extended statistics directly, dependencies were applied clause by clause in a fixed order and only on the inner relation, and he proposed handling all join clauses for a pair of relations at once in extended_stats.c. The author agreed it could be done better but posted no new version. In July the patch no longer compiled, and it still did not one commitfest later, so it was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: The patch includes some *very* interesting ideas, but I think it's does them too late and at the wrong level of abstraction.

precedents_retrieved.title: Patch to implement missing join selectivity estimation for range types
precedents_retrieved.authors: Mahmoud SAKR (mahmsakr), Diogo Repas (diogo.repas), Maxime Schoemans (mschoema), Zhicheng Luo (zcsysu.163.com)
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Tom Lane, vignesh C, jian he, Tomas Vondra
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds join selectivity estimation for range and multirange operators such as <<, >>, &&, &<, &>, @> and <@, using the existing bounds histograms instead of the constant 0.005. A multirange is treated as its bounding range.
precedents_retrieved.objection: After the January 2024 revision, the CFBot still showed an AddressSanitizer abort in calc_hist_join_selectivity, and the authors did not post a fix. The function was still duplicated in rangetypes_selfuncs.c and multirangetypes_selfuncs.c, which Tomas Vondra, Tom Lane and jian he asked to remove. jian he also asked for estimate-ratio tests in place of the 3-way join plans, and the thread ends with no reply from the authors.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I also agree with the upthread criticism that having two identical functions in different source files will be a maintenance nightmare.

precedents_retrieved.title: Plan a filtering inner join as a semijoin
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds convert_joins_to_semijoins(), which turns an inner join whose righthand relation only filters rows into a JOIN_SEMI SpecialJoinInfo when the query discards duplicates. It is limited to a single-relation righthand side and is controlled by enable_semijoin_conversion.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that the planner normally converts semijoins to inner joins to gain join-order flexibility, and that converting the other way removes it. The author agreed that the patch makes a rewrite-time decision that should be made on cost, and withdrew it. He replaced it with a new patch that builds a second relation and lets it compete on cost during the join search.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Normally we try
to convert semijoins to inner joins in order to gain join-order
flexibility.  I can't see a good reason to go in the other direction.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. [P1] (LEFT JOIN removal via DISTINCT, stopped on volatility checks) and [P2] (inner join removal via foreign keys and an AlternativePlan node) share keywords only, and their recorded reasons do not apply to skipping a join whose inner rel is already dummy. Message #1 does not mention any earlier discussion of this idea.
The patch adds no syntax, no GUC, no catalog object and nothing pg_dump must handle. Changed plans and EXPLAIN output on master are the intended effect and follow existing join-removal practice.

The patch changes only planner path generation in joinrels.c and adds no persistent or cross-node state: no WAL, on-disk, catalog, protocol or exported struct changes. The "stable" target and plan changes in minor releases fall under other angles, since nothing here blocks a back-patch on ABI grounds.

The proposal has no privilege or exposure aspect, so this angle has no objection. It is a planner-only change to paths and row estimates in joinrels.c, with no new SQL, GUC, function or catalog. Privilege checks on the dropped inner rel come from the range table, as with existing left join removal, and the only quals involved are "innervar IS NULL", which call no user functions, so RLS and leakproofness are not affected.
Hot-path cost looks small, since the check runs only when the inner rel is already dummy. The objections above focus on back-patching, fragility, and the choice of design.

Postgres has no existing way to get this result. Left join removal in analyzejoins.c runs before relation sizes are set and dummy rels are known, and it does not apply here because the IS NULL qual uses an inner Var. set_join_pathlist_hook can add paths but cannot fix the joinrel row estimate, which is the main gain. Rewriting the query is not possible when pruning empties the inner rel at plan time.
The one objection asks for evidence of demand. Costs appear to fall only on queries with a dummy inner rel, so the main cost is maintenance, not planning time for everyone.
